verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev documents writing workflows as plain async TypeScript rather than a DSL (docs-2, docs-40), and says it uses checkpoint-resume to run normal TypeScript with no determinism constraints (docs-38). A community user confirms moving from n8n's GUI to code in the IDE (comm-2). Automatic retries complement durability (docs-4), but the language is limited to TypeScript/JavaScript, with Python only via a build extension (docs-43). Missing for 10: detailed documentation of step-level checkpointing semantics (what is persisted and when), first-class support beyond TS/JS, and independent hands-on corroboration of checkpoint-resume behavior.
